Name: Requiring outreach, surveys, and reporting related to the effects of chatbot use on mental health.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring outreach, surveys, and reporting related to the effects of chatbot use on mental health
BodyName: Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council

Summary: This bill would require the Commissioner of Health and Mental Hygiene to conduct a public awareness campaign on the negative mental health effects associated with chatbot use. As part of the public awareness campaign, the Commissioner would be required to develop specific materials for young people, older adults, and veterans. Additionally, the Commissioner would be required to conduct triennial citywide surveys on the mental health of chatbot users in the city. The Commissioner would be required to publish an annual report that includes agency actions, proposals, and current research addressing mental health effects of chatbot use; a summary of any mental health emergencies due to chatbot use in the city during the past year; and, if applicable, the results of that year’s citywide mental health survey.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 1 of title 17 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 17-199.35 to read as follows:
§ 17.199.35 Mental health effects of chatbot use. a. Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the term “chatbot” means an artificial intelligence system that engages in interactive, natural-language communication with a user and generates or selects content in response to user inputs including text or voice.
b. Public awareness and outreach campaign. 1. No later than 180 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall implement a public awareness and outreach campaign regarding the negative mental health effects associated with chatbot use. As part of such campaign, the commissioner shall develop and disseminate materials that include:
(a) A description of negative health and social consequences associated with chatbot use, including psychosis, suicidal ideation, distorted decision-making, social isolation, and potential for self-injury or self-harm; 
(b) A description of ways that chatbots encourage prolonged use, including sycophancy, interpersonal continuity, and frictionless exchange;
(c) Ways to detect overreliance or dependence on conversational chatbot usage by oneself or another;
(d) Resources available for individuals experiencing overreliance or dependence on a chatbot; and
(e) Best practices to safely use chatbots.
2. The commissioner shall develop versions of the materials required pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision that are tailored to individuals under the age of 24, individuals over the age of 60, and veterans, and disseminate the materials to the targeted populations. 
3. The commissioner shall post all materials produced pursuant to this subdivision on the department’s website. At least annually, the commissioner shall review the information contained in the materials and update or add to the materials as necessary to ensure accuracy and utility.
c. Survey. No later than 180 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and triennially thereafter, the commissioner shall conduct a citywide survey regarding the use of chatbots by residents of the city, and the effects of such use on the mental health and wellbeing of such residents. 
d. Reporting. No later than 1 year after the effective date of the law that enacted this section, and annually thereafter, the commissioner shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and publish on the department’s website, a report that includes, at a minimum:
1. A summary of activities performed by the commissioner related to addressing mental health effects of chatbot use;
2. An overview of contemporary research relating to the effects of chatbots on the mental health and wellbeing of chatbot users;
3. A summary of any mental health emergencies related to the use of a chatbot that occurred in the city during the past calendar year; 
4. Any proposals for policies or initiatives to address the negative mental health effects of chatbot use; and
5. If the commissioner conducted a citywide survey pursuant to subdivision c of this section during the preceding year, the results of such survey, and an analysis of such results.
§ 3. This law takes effect immediately.
